1. Open the starwars dataset (located in tidyverse)
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
data("starwars")
```

2. Create a scatter plot of character's height and mass. 
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(jtools)
library(Rmisc)

ggplot(starwars, aes(x = mass, y = height))+geom_point(na.rm = TRUE)+theme_classic()

```

2a. Change the color and shape of the points in your scatter plot. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(x = mass, y = height))+geom_point(na.rm = TRUE, color = "purple", shape = 6)+theme_classic()
```

3. Add Homeworld as a third variable to your scatterplot. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(x = mass, y = height, color = homeworld))+geom_point(na.rm = TRUE)+theme_classic()
```

3a. What do you notice about the graph? (e.g. describe what you see)
```{r}
#In my view, R automatically assigned different colors to different categories(homeworld).To me, it feels overwhelming and the graph has some readability issue. Hard to interpret. 
```

4. Make a boxplot of height. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(y = height))+geom_boxplot(na.rm = TRUE)+theme_apa()+ylab("Height(cm)")
```

5. Make a boxplot of height for each species present in the data. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(x = species, y = height))+geom_boxplot(na.rm = TRUE)+theme_apa()+xlab("Species")+ylab("Height(cm)")

```

5a. change the appearance of your graph in at least 3 ways. 
```{r}
#Add title and change theme
ggplot(starwars, aes(x = species, y = height))+geom_boxplot(na.rm = TRUE)+theme_classic()+xlab("Species")+ylab("Height(cm)")+ggtitle("Height Distibutions by Species in Starwars")

#Assign color to each species
library(viridis)

ggplot(starwars, aes(x = species, y = height, fill = species))+geom_boxplot(na.rm = TRUE)+scale_fill_viridis(discrete = TRUE, option = "magma")+theme_classic()+xlab("Species")+ylab("Height(cm)")+ggtitle("Height Distibutions by Species in Starwars")

#Change the font for title, labels, category names
ggplot(starwars, aes(x = species, y = height, fill = species))+geom_boxplot(na.rm = TRUE)+scale_fill_viridis(discrete = TRUE, option = "magma")+theme_classic()+xlab("Species")+ylab("Height(cm)")+ggtitle("Height Distibutions by Species in Starwars")+theme(text = element_text(family = "serif", size = 15))

```

6. Using any variables in the starwars dataset, create a graph that uses a color palette from viridis.
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(x = skin_color, y = eye_color, color = hair_color))+geom_jitter(na.rm = TRUE)+scale_fill_viridis(discrete = TRUE, option = "rocket")+theme_apa()

```

7.Using any variables in the starwars dataset, create a graph that uses a color palette from RColorBrewer.
```{r}
library(RColorBrewer)

ggplot(starwars, aes(x = birth_year, y = height, color = sex))+geom_jitter(na.rm = TRUE)+scale_color_brewer(palette = "BrBG")+theme_classic()

```

8. Using any variables in the starwars dataset, create a graph using facet_wrap
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(x = mass, y = height))+geom_point(na.rm = TRUE)+theme_classic()+facet_wrap("gender")

#Added labels for each. 

labels_for_graph<- c(masculine = "Masculine Characters", feminine = "Feminine Characeters")

ggplot(starwars, aes(x = mass, y = height))+geom_point(na.rm = TRUE)+theme_classic()+facet_wrap("gender", labeller=as_labeller(labels_for_graph))+xlab("Mass")+ylab("Height")+ggtitle("Mass and Height Distribution for Masculine and Feminine Characters")

```
